invariants.rationale: The method calls newText.equals(oldText), which would throw NullPointerException if newText is null. Thus, oldText can be null, but typically both should be non-null unless explicitly allowed.
newText.equals(oldText) requires newText to be non-null, or else a NullPointerException will occur.
If newText equals oldText, the method immediately returns false without changing any state.
If the contents are considered equal, sometimes string references can be the same (trivial identity aspect), though not always guaranteed by equals.
Although two strings can have the same content but different references, the method could be called with either the same or different instances. This invariant checks their reference identity.
